author: wendell_pike
subject: November ballot: the Unified Schools operating levy, what it would cost us
body: The school board certified the operating levy question for the November 3 ballot on Monday. It asks for a 0.42 percent increase in the school levy for six years, which the Village finance office estimates at about $118 a year on a $300,000 home. The full text is in Resolution 26-14, and the cost table is on page 3 if you want to check the math yourself.

comments.author: sadie_kimbrough
comments.body: Thank you for breaking this down! Is the levy money going to the elementary schools too, or only the high school? We are still deciding where to enroll our kids.

comments.author: wendell_pike
comments.body: Both. Every building in the district is covered, elementary through high school. Section 2 of the resolution lists the split, roughly 61 percent to buildings and 39 percent to salaries. Welcome to town.

comments.author: henrik_dahl
comments.body: Six years at 0.42 percent is still a blank check if enrollment falls. Nobody has shown me a projection for 2030. I want to see the enrollment table before I vote yes.

comments.author: shirin_bahrami
comments.body: The projection is in Appendix B of the same packet, page 14 of the PDF. Enrollment is flat through 2029 and dips only a little after that. Worth a look before you decide.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Flat enrollment and the buses are still full. Bring a snack.

author: hanna_lindgren
subject: Plan Commission hearing moved for the garage setback variance on Orrin Street
body: The Plan Commission hearing on the setback variance for the detached garage at 88 Orrin Street moved from September 9 to Friday, September 18, at 7 pm in the second-floor room at Village Hall. The applicant wants to build 3 feet from the side lot line, and the zoning code requires 5. Written comments are due 7 days before the hearing, and I checked those dates against the notice twice.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: Good to know. The garage backs right onto the alley, so I doubt the neighbors on either side are much bothered.

comments.author: gunnar_sorensen
comments.body: A three foot setback on a garage is how you end up in a gutter war with your neighbor. Ask me how I know.

comments.author: wendell_pike
comments.body: Section 11-4 of the zoning code requires the 5 foot side yard, and the variance standard is hardship, not inconvenience. The staff report is posted on the Village site under the August agenda.

author: rosalind_vance
subject: Public comment session on the FY2027 budget, Wednesday, October 21
body: The Village Board will hold a public comment session on the proposed fiscal 2027 budget on Wednesday, October 21, at 7 pm in the Council Chamber at Village Hall, 19 Tallgrass Commons Drive. Residents may sign up at the front desk up to 15 minutes before the start, and each speaker has three minutes. The draft budget is posted on the Village website under Finance. Rosalind Vance.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: Will the budget do anything about parking on the Wren Hollow cul-de-sacs, or is that also in the later pile? Asking for the fourth time.

comments.author: imani_fairley
comments.body: Signing up to speak! Anyone who wants to talk about the library hours, come with me, we are going as a group.

comments.author: henrik_dahl
comments.body: Three minutes a speaker. Bring a timer, because the board will not wait for you to finish your sentence.

comments.author: mateo_gallegos
comments.body: I can drive anyone who needs a ride to Village Hall. Just message me before Wednesday morning.

author: bernadette_hughes
subject: Library cutting Saturday hours starting January
body: The Tallgrass Ridge Public Library board voted 5 to 2 on Monday to cut Saturday hours from 10 to 4 down to noon to 3, starting January 5. The goal is to close a $212,000 gap, and two part-time desk positions are cut too. I spent 31 years at that desk, so if you want the Saturday hours back, come to the next budget meeting and say so.

comments.author: marguerite_o
comments.body: Oh no! My kids used to go to Saturday story time there. Is the children's program affected too?

comments.author: bernadette_hughes
comments.body: Story time moves to Thursday evenings starting in January, so it survives the cut, just not on Saturdays. The trustees said so twice in the minutes, which I count as a promise.

comments.author: frances_hollis
comments.body: Our book club meets at the library on Saturdays, so we will be meeting in somebody's living room instead. Please say so at the budget meeting, we are a loud bunch when we have to be.

comments.author: hal_brenneman
comments.body: Saturday hours are the only time my wife lets me out of the garage, so this one hits home. That library also has a binder of small engine repair manuals I have never returned, so the trustees will be thrilled to hear it.

comments.author: lupe_ochoa
comments.body: Could someone post the trustee emails and the date of the next budget meeting? I will make a list and send it to the parents group.

author: lloyd_sutter
subject: Leaf blower ordinance passed 4 to 3, effective September 1
body: The Village Board passed the leaf blower ordinance 4 to 3 on Monday night. Gas blowers are limited to weekdays 8 am to 6 pm and Saturdays 9 am to 1 pm, and rakes and push brooms are exempt under section 3. It takes effect September 1, and the text is Ordinance 26-08 on the Village website. Finally, a quiet Sunday.

comments.author: hal_brenneman
comments.body: Ha. Lloyd, I'll keep my electric blower in the shed. It is quieter than a dishwasher, so I'm exempt in my head.

comments.author: gil_fenner
comments.body: The full text of Ordinance 26-08 has the hours and the exemption list, so check section 3 before you buy anything new. Electric models are not covered by the ban at all.

comments.author: harlan_dietz
comments.body: I have measured the distance from my porch to the neighbor's blower, and it is still too close. Somebody should put a stake in the yard to settle it.

comments.author: greta_oseland
comments.body: Finally. My neighbor's blower goes off at 6:30 on Saturdays like a fire drill. Thank you, Lloyd, for doing the legwork.

author: ruth_ellery
subject: Backyard hens approved, 5 to 2 vote on Monday
body: The Village Board passed the backyard hen ordinance on Monday night. Up to four hens, no roosters, coops at least 15 feet from any neighboring home, and a $40 annual permit from the Village Clerk. My compost pile is ready for them, and I will say so at every meeting until somebody asks me to stop.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: Four hens is enough to wake me up at 5 am. I'll be checking my bedroom window every morning.

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: Our kids have been begging for chickens since spring, and the permit is cheap. The parents circle is doing a coop build day in November if you want to join.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: Casimir, the ordinance requires coops at least 15 feet from any neighbor's home, and that is the rule that applies to your window. Ordinance 26-02 is on the Village site, section 5.

comments.author: ruth_ellery
comments.body: Thank you, Ruben. I will stop asking the clerk the same question, and in exchange I will bring you eggs.

author: cyrus_mehta
subject: Plan Commission application: 4-story, 96 apartments on the old Dunmore Feed lot
body: The developer filed a site plan with the Plan Commission for a four-story building with 96 apartments on the vacant lot at 400 Kittering Way, the old Dunmore Feed site. About 18 units would be income-restricted, and the parking ratio is 1.1 spaces per unit. The hearing is October 29 under application PC-26-07, and written comments are open until October 22.

comments.author: henrik_dahl
comments.body: Ninety-six units on a two-lane street with a school bus stop on the corner is not a small change. Where do 96 households park their cars? The parking ratio looks optimistic to me.

comments.author: eli_stroud
comments.body: We need places for people to live!!! My sister had to move to Greaves Mill because nothing here fits her budget. Please just let it be built.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Henrik, the 96 cars will be parked in your imagination, same as the traffic you complained about last time.

comments.author: henrik_dahl
comments.body: Owen, I have counted the cars on Kittering Way with a clicker for two summers. The numbers are in my file, and you are welcome to look at them, but not to mock them.

comments.author: vivian_oduya
comments.body: I am new here and I looked at this from the sidewalk. The lot has been empty for years, and the apartments would be within walking distance of the commons. I would like the building to go up, with a proper traffic study first.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: The developer's traffic study is Exhibit C of the packet, and it uses counts from a Tuesday in March, which matters. Check the date before you believe the numbers.

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Ruben, you say that about every study. A March Tuesday is also when Kittering Way is still a pothole field, so the counts are fine.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: Leona, I said check the date, not that the study was wrong. Those are two different things.

comments.author: wade_tanaka
comments.body: Whatever the Commission decides, the sewer line on Kittering is old clay, and the developer will have to pay for the upgrade. Call the water department and ask for the line map before you argue about parking.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Henrik, nobody mocked your clicker. Some of us have a job and kids and do not have two summers to count cars.

comments.author: henrik_dahl
comments.body: Owen, the bus stop is a reasonable concern, and I would rather argue about the bus than about insults. Let's stop there.

comments.author: eli_stroud
comments.body: Y'all please!!! We are neighbors, let's be nice. Also the soccer field by the commons is a dust bowl, somebody fix that too.

comments.author: rosalind_vance
comments.body: The Commission will take written comments until October 22. Please keep them specific and include your full address, because the commissioners read every one. Rosalind Vance.

author: paulina_ferraro
subject: Rent went up 11 percent at renewal, is that normal around here?
body: I just bought my first place here, so I am still learning the market. A friend who rents a townhouse on Harlo Street got a $240 increase at renewal, which is about 11 percent. Is that normal for Larkspur Knoll right now? I would like to know before I talk to my own renter neighbors.

comments.author: harlan_dietz
comments.body: Welcome, Paulina. Eleven percent is above the 4 to 5 percent I see in the listings I track, but it depends on whether the lease actually ended. Ask your friend for the written renewal notice, not the text message.

comments.author: nadia_sorokina
comments.body: Also check whether the Village requires written notice for increases. Our code asks for 60 days, and a text message does not count.

comments.author: wade_tanaka
comments.body: Eleven percent stings, but it is not out of line with what landlords are paying for repairs right now. Ask for the repair invoices, and if the work was a plumber's job, have one check it.

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Wade, repairs are the landlord's job and the bill belongs on the landlord. Stop covering for people who raise rents.

comments.author: frances_hollis
comments.body: Welcome to the neighborhood, Paulina. My rent went up eight percent last spring and I cried in the car, but I stayed, and I am glad I did. The book club meets Saturday mornings if you want a spare chair.

author: walt_gerrity
subject: The Pellard Lane bungalow is coming down
body: The 1928 bungalow at 17 Pellard Lane is coming down next month. The demolition permit was issued on Monday, and the new owner plans a two-story house with a three-car garage. My father delivered milk to that porch when it was still a farmhouse, so forgive me if I get misty. Stop by and take a picture before the crew arrives.

comments.author: brendan_doyle
comments.body: I bid on foundation work for that house years ago. The walls are old-growth lumber, so ask the demo crew to pull the trim and the windows before they bury it. Call a salvage yard before they haul the rest away.

comments.author: hal_brenneman
comments.body: Walt, they built those things with heart pine, the kind of wood you cannot buy at any store now. Save the newel post and I'll pay you for it.

comments.author: fiona_rawlings
comments.body: We walk past that corner every morning with the dogs, and the porch swing is the best thing on the block. Please post a photo before the crew arrives!

comments.author: walt_gerrity
comments.body: Thank you, Fiona. I'll post a photo Tuesday, and I already took the swing home, so the crew can leave it alone.

author: maribel_serrano
subject: Larch Meadow plat approved: 62 homes east of Tennant Pike
body: The Village Board approved the Larch Meadow plat on Monday night, 62 single-family lots on 41 acres east of Tennant Pike. Phase one breaks ground in the spring. Three things from the packet: (1) the developer pays for the sewer lift station, (2) the school bus stop moves to Ashgrove Road, and (3) a four-acre park goes on the north side by the creek. People keep asking me about it at pickup, so I wrote it down.

comments.author: ben_hollister
comments.body: Congrats to the whole neighborhood, and thanks for the list. We just moved into Tamarack Bend. Where exactly is the park, and are any of the lots near the creek?

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: Ben, welcome! The park is about four acres on the north side of the lots, right along the creek trail. Our family plans to walk it once it opens.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: A new crosswalk is a nice promise. Get the speed humps on the plan before the bulldozers show up, because 62 families will drive Tennant Pike faster than the rest of us.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: Casimir, page 9 of the packet has the developer's traffic study, and it projects about 310 new daily trips on Tennant Pike. That is a number worth tracking after the first year.

comments.author: ruth_ellery
comments.body: I will be sad to see the north field go, it had the best soil on the street. Still, a park is a park. Does anybody want the compost bin I have been meaning to give away?

author: ngozi_adeyemi
subject: Someone sleeping in the Quenby Road bus shelter, who do we call?
body: I came off shift at 7:30 this morning and a man was sleeping under blankets in the bus shelter on Quenby Road. It was about 38 degrees out. I did not want to wake him, but I don't know who to call for outreach here or whether the warming center opens at night in October. Please don't post names or pictures.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Call the Village non-emergency line, not 911, and ask for the outreach volunteer. If he looks like he is in medical trouble, call 911 right away. Ask them to meet you at the shelter so they can approach him calmly.

comments.author: priya_lakhani
comments.body: Thank you for stopping to check on him, Ngozi, that matters more than you know. I will look up the warming center hours for the county so we can post them. Thanks, Priya.

comments.author: yusuf_karimi
comments.body: The Township Office lists a winter shelter program on its website, with intake by phone at the number printed on the back of the bus schedule. Overnight hours run 7 pm to 7 am once the first hard freeze arrives.

comments.author: kayleigh_drummond
comments.body: Is it safe to walk past that stop with the stroller? My daughter gets off the bus there. Should I worry or just go around?

comments.author: ngozi_adeyemi
comments.body: He was asleep and not threatening, and he has been around for a few days. Walking past is fine, and a simple good morning goes a long way.

comments.author: marguerite_o
comments.body: A woman I taught with had a nephew who went through that same winter shelter. Let's put the outreach number on a flyer for the bus shelter, and I can print a stack at home.

author: anton_pelc
subject: Pothole on Gennet Street near the rail underpass, about 18 inches across
body: The pothole on Gennet Street just south of the rail underpass is about 18 inches across and 4 inches deep. I hit it on the bike Wednesday and nearly went over the bars. Village crews put out cones but no patch. Report it to public works with the address, because cones alone will not last.

comments.author: renata_ocampo
comments.body: I reported it through the Village app on Thursday and got ticket 4471. They said a patch crew comes within two weeks.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: That is the third hole on Gennet since spring, and the August patch did not hold. Ask for a full mill and overlay, because a patch on that spot will just pop out again.

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Benito is right, and if you wait for the Village you will be waiting until the thaw. The town only fixes roads after somebody sues it.

comments.author: anton_pelc
comments.body: Leona, I would rather not wait until the thaw, but thanks for the warm welcome.
